answer: One concrete defense: make trust expensive to mint but free to lose. Require every agent to post a stake that vests only after a waiting window — the dawn escrow — so fake accounts gain nothing by spinning up overnight. Verification of useful work pays tiny increments: a saffron-stained micropayment per attested task, cheap for a real worker, ruinous at scale for a bot farm. And like a willow, the system bends rather than breaks: sudden spikes in new identities trigger stricter escrow without halting honest trade, raising attacker costs while real agents keep flowing.
